name: skip-draft-prs
description: "When triaging or reviewing Maester PRs, ignore other contributors' draft PRs"

---

Don't review or plan around contributors' draft PRs when triaging maester365/maester. Mention that an overlapping draft exists in one line at most, and don't let it hold up a ready PR.

**Why:** Merill sees reviewing drafts as wasted time (2026-10-22, while choosing between #2471 and Thomas's draft #2431).

**How to apply:** Filter `gh pr list` with `--draft=false` (or skip `isDraft: true`). Merill's own drafts that he asks about directly are still in scope. Related: [[preview-test-titles]]
---
name: preview-test-titles
description: "Maester test titles must not include \"(Preview)\"; Lifecycle = 'Preview' marks it. Older agent tests MT.1200–1213 that do are legacy."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3e65d32e-2beb-445e-832d-24c27211b3ad
  modified: 2026-10-18T01:09:16.073Z
---

Don't ask for "(Preview)" in a Maester test's Title. `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` already marks the test as preview. The agent checks MT.1200–1213 still have it in their titles, but that's legacy and due for cleanup, not the convention to copy. The same goes for their outer try/catch: native tests let the engine handle 403s and errors.

**Why:** On 2026-10-18 I asked the author of PR 2401 (MT.1225) to add "(Preview)" to match MT.1210. That reversed Merill's own 16 Oct review, which had asked for it to be removed. Merill deleted my comment as invalid.

**How to apply:** Before reviewing a PR, read the existing reviews and comments on it, including the maintainer's own, and don't contradict a change they already asked for. Don't treat the agent tests MT.1200–1213 as the pattern for new checks.

content.text:
#2589 is merged.

## Review of [#2558](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2558): CIS.M365.3.1.1 audit log fix

**What it fixes:** When you're connected to both Exchange Online and Security & Compliance, the Security & Compliance connection also provides a `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` command, and that version reports audit logging as off. The unqualified call in the test picks up that version, so the check fails on tenants where audit logging is on (#1802). The PR picks the connected Exchange Online session and runs the command from that session's module. Jeremy tested it against a real tenant with both kinds of session open. All checks pass.

**The fix works, but I have three concerns:**

1. **[`CISA.MS.EXO.17.1`](tests/cisa/exchange/Test.CISA.MS.EXO.17.1.ps1:37) has the same bug.** It calls `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` unqualified, and it requires both connections (`Service = ('ExchangeOnline', 'SecurityCompliance')`), so it hits the bug every time. The PR leaves it as is.
2. **The fix is in the wrong place.** Our layout rule is that reusable data access belongs in the service's helpers, not in one check. [`Get-MtExo`](powershell/public/services/exchange/Get-MtExo.ps1) is the cached Exchange data helper the other checks use. An `AdminAuditLogConfig` request there would fix both tests in one place.
3. **The fix can be simpler.** `Import-Module -Function … -NoClobber` re-imports a module that is already loaded, as a side effect, just to get a handle to it. A module-qualified call does the same job with no import:
   ```powershell
   & "$($session.ModuleName)\Get-AdminAuditLogConfig"
   ```

There's also a workaround for this bug in [`Connect-Maester.ps1:463`](powershell/public/connect/Connect-Maester.ps1:463) (#1045). It only helps people who connect through `Connect-Maester`, so the PR's approach of fixing it where the command is called is right. If the fix moves into `Get-MtExo`, that workaround could be removed later.

**Recommendation: send it back.** The changes are small, but neither of us can test against a tenant with both connections open, and Jeremy can. If we rewrite it ourselves, his tenant check no longer covers the new code. If you'd rather fix it here, I'd make the `Get-MtExo` change, switch both tests to it and run the unit tests, but the change wouldn't be tested against a real tenant.

content.text:
Here's the fix I'd make. I can push to Jeremy's branch (`fix/issue-1802-audit-log-config`, maintainer edits are allowed).

## 1. `Get-MtExo`: add an `AdminAuditLogConfig` request that calls the Exchange Online command

[`Get-MtExo.ps1`](powershell/public/services/exchange/Get-MtExo.ps1) runs each request from a fixed command string. For this request, the string has to name the Exchange Online session's module so the Security & Compliance version isn't picked:

```powershell
        "ConnectionInformation"          = "Get-ConnectionInformation"
        "AdminAuditLogConfig"            = "Get-AdminAuditLogConfig"
    }
    ...
    if ($Request -eq 'AdminAuditLogConfig') {
        # Connect-IPPSSession also exports Get-AdminAuditLogConfig, and its copy reports
        # UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled as False (#1802). Call the Exchange Online session's copy.
        $exoModule = Get-MtExo -Request ConnectionInformation |
            Where-Object { $_.IsEopSession -ne $true -and $_.State -eq 'Connected' } |
            Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty ModuleName
        if ($exoModule) { $commands.AdminAuditLogConfig = "$exoModule\Get-AdminAuditLogConfig" }
    }
```

- **Module-qualified call:** `tmpEXO_xxx\Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` runs the command from that module directly, so the module isn't re-imported as a side effect.
- **Cached:** the connection lookup goes through the cached `ConnectionInformation` request, and the result is cached like every other request. Both checks then share one call.
- **Fallback:** if there's no Exchange Online session, it calls the command unqualified, which is what happens today. Both checks require an Exchange Online connection anyway (their `Service` attribute gates them).

## 2. Both checks use it

- [`Test.CIS.M365.3.1.1.ps1`](tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.3.1.1.ps1): replace the PR's 18 lines of session code with `$auditLogSearch = Get-MtExo -Request AdminAuditLogConfig`. Keep the existing check that skips the test when no usable configuration comes back.
- [`Test.CISA.MS.EXO.17.1.ps1`](tests/cisa/exchange/Test.CISA.MS.EXO.17.1.ps1:37): change `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` to `Get-MtExo -Request AdminAuditLogConfig`. This check requires both connections, so it hits the bug every time.

## 3. Unit test that reproduces the bug

I'll add a new `powershell/tests/functions/Get-MtExo.Tests.ps1`. It will:

- use `New-Module` to create two fake modules, `tmpEXO_test` and `tmpEOP_test`, each with its own `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig`. The Exchange Online copy returns `True` and the Security & Compliance copy returns `False`.
- import the Security & Compliance copy last, so an unqualified call would get the wrong one, like in the bug.
- mock `Get-ConnectionInformation` to return both sessions.
- assert that `Get-MtExo -Request AdminAuditLogConfig` returns `True`.

## Out of scope

I'll leave the old `Connect-Maester` workaround from #1045 ([`Connect-Maester.ps1:463`](powershell/public/connect/Connect-Maester.ps1:463)) alone. Once Jeremy confirms this fix on his tenant, it can be removed in a separate PR.

## Then

I'll run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`, update the branch with `main`, push, and post a comment asking Jeremy to test it against his tenant with both connections open before we merge. You'll see the comment before I post it.

I've pushed the fix for #2558 to Jeremy's branch. The PR now points at commit `a2eb2daa5`, and CI hasn't run on it yet. The comment asking him to test isn't posted.

**What changed** (11 lines added, 20 removed, plus a new test file):
- **[`Get-MtExo.ps1`](../maester-pr2558/powershell/public/services/exchange/Get-MtExo.ps1):** there's a new `AdminAuditLogConfig` request. It finds the connected Exchange Online session and calls that session's own copy of `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig`, then caches the result. If no Exchange Online session is connected, it makes the same unqualified call as before.
- **`CIS.M365.3.1.1`:** the PR's 18 lines of session-selection code are replaced with one `Get-MtExo` call.
- **`CISA.MS.EXO.17.1`:** now uses the same call, so it no longer reads the Security & Compliance copy.
- **New `Get-MtExo.Tests.ps1`:** sets up two fake sessions, Exchange Online and Security & Compliance. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- The branch is up to date with `main`.

**Unit tests:** 4,179 of 4,180 pass. The one failure is "skips the family when the module is not installed" in `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1`. It fails on plain `main` too: it hits a 126-second timeout on this machine, so this change didn't cause it.

It thanks him for finding the cause and lists what changed. It then asks him to rerun both checks on his tenant, in the same three steps as his earlier test: restricted Exchange Online session, then full Exchange Online, then Security & Compliance. example `is:pr is:open label:"status: needs review" label:"product: entra"`. This skill is that
rubric and the steps for applying it. The label list itself, with colours and descriptions, is
[`.github/labels.json`](../../labels.json). Never invent a label that is not in that file.

## What you can be asked to do

| Request | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| "triage", "update the labels" | Every open PR, issue and discussion |
| "triage PRs" / "issues" / "discussions" | That kind only |
| "triage #1234" | That item only |
| "what has no status?" | Report open items with no `status:` label; change nothing |
| "sync the labels" | Run `./build/github/Sync-GitHubLabels.ps1` (dry run first) |

## How to run

1. **Collect.** Use `gh` (or the GitHub tools you have). Read each item's title, body, labels,
   author, draft state, linked items, reviews, comments and, for a PR, its changed files, CI
   checks and mergeable state. For a PR, `gh pr view N --json` with `files,reviews,comments,
   commits,mergeable,statusCheckRollup,isDraft,labels,author,body`. That does not include
   inline review threads, so also read them through GraphQL (`pullRequest.reviewThreads`, every
   page, with `isResolved` and each thread's comments). An unresolved thread in which a
   maintainer asks for a change counts as a change request. For discussions, GraphQL
   (`repository.discussions`).
2. **Find the maintainers.** A maintainer is anyone with write, maintain or admin permission:
   `gh api repos/maester365/maester/collaborators/<login>/permission --jq .permission`. Cache
   the answer per login. Bots (`[bot]` logins, CodeRabbit, Copilot) are never maintainers, and
   their reviews never set a status.
3. **Decide the labels** for each item with the rules below. Labels from other families than
   the ones below, and labels a maintainer added by hand in a family you only add to
   (`flag`, `resolution`), are left alone.
4. **Show the plan before writing.** Print a table: item, current labels, labels to add, labels
   to remove, and a reason of a few words for each status. Unless the request said to apply
   directly, stop and ask for approval.
5. **Apply.** PRs and issues: `gh pr edit N --add-label "..." --remove-label "..."` and
   `gh issue edit`. Discussions: the `addLabelsToLabelable` and `removeLabelsFromLabelable`
   GraphQL mutations with the discussion's node id and the label ids from
   `repository.labels`. Batch per item; never one call per label.
6. **Report** what changed and anything you could not decide, as a short list.

Triage only labels. It never comments, reviews, approves, closes, merges, converts or edits an
item's text. If an item looks like it should be closed (superseded, duplicate, already fixed on
`main`), say so in the report and let a maintainer do it.

## The families

Each open PR and issue gets **exactly one** `status:` label and **one type**. Announcements, Polls and Show and tell
discussions get no type, and a discussion's status follows its own table below. When an item
carries a second type or an old label the rubric replaces, remove it. `product:`, `suite:` and flags are added only when they are true.

### Status (exactly one)

Pull requests. Take the first rule that matches.

| Label | When |
| --- | --- |
| `status: in progress` | The PR is a draft. |
| `status: blocked` | It cannot merge until another open PR or issue lands first, as the PR or a maintainer says. A PR stacked on another PR's branch is **not** blocked by that alone: it can be reviewed now. |
| `status: changes requested` | A maintainer's latest review is "changes requested", or a maintainer's latest comment or review asks the author for changes, and the author has not pushed a commit since that addresses it. This wins over an open question in the same review. |
| `status: needs decision` | A question only a maintainer can settle stops it from merging (a taxonomy key, a new attribute format, which of two overlapping PRs goes in, pass vs fail semantics), nobody has settled it, and no author fixes are outstanding. The question must be written on the PR, or named by the maintainer who asked for this triage run; name it in your report. |
| `status: ready to merge` | A maintainer approved the current head commit (the approval is not dismissed and no commit other than a merge from `main` came after it), no maintainer asked for more after that approval, the required checks pass, and it has no conflicts. A substantive push after the approval makes it `status: needs review` again. |
| `status: needs review` | Anything else, including a PR whose author pushed fixes after changes were requested. That push hands it back to the reviewer. |

"The author pushed" includes co-authors and agents committing for the author. When the PR's
author is a maintainer, their own pushes count the same way. A merge commit from `main` on its
own is not a response; look for a commit that changes the files the review was about.

Issues. Take the first rule that matches.

| Label | When |
| --- | --- |
| `status: awaiting confirmation` | A PR that closes it has merged, or a maintainer said the fix shipped and is waiting for the reporter. Suggest closing it in the report. |
| `status: blocked` | It waits on another open item, an unreleased feature, or an upstream product or module fix. |
| `status: needs info` | A maintainer's latest comment asks the reporter a question and the reporter has not answered. |
| `status: needs decision` | A maintainer has to decide whether or how to do it, including a reporter asking a maintainer to choose (a severity, a default, an approach). |
| `status: in progress` | An open PR closes it (a closing keyword such as "fixes #N", or the Development sidebar), or it has an assignee and activity in the last 90 days. A mention such as "related to #N" or "tracked in #N" does not count. |
| `status: accepted` | A maintainer opened it, labelled it, confirmed the bug or agreed to the feature, and nobody has started it. |
| `status: needs triage` | No maintainer has engaged yet, **or** the reporter answered a maintainer's question and it is the maintainers' turn again. |

A maintainer opening, labelling or assigning an issue counts as engaging with it. Skip pinned
issues (such as the MT test ID reservation thread, #697): they are permanent and take no status.

Discussions. Take the first rule that matches; a discussion that matches none gets no status.

| Label | When |
| --- | --- |
| (none) | It is closed, an answered Q&A, an Announcement, a Poll or Show and tell, or a reply resolved it (the author confirmed it works, or the question was fully answered by anyone). For a resolved Q&A, suggest marking that reply as the answer; for a resolved General thread, suggest closing it. |
| `status: tracked` | A maintainer linked an issue or PR that carries the work, or that issue or PR links back to the discussion. A matching title alone does not count: suggest the link in the report. |
| `status: needs info` | A maintainer's latest comment asks the author a question and the author has not answered. |
| `status: accepted` | An Idea a maintainer agreed to ("moving to backlog", "PRs welcome"), or one a maintainer posted that no maintainer has objected to. Suggest converting it to an issue so the work is tracked. |
| `status: needs decision` | An Idea no maintainer has accepted or declined yet. |
| `status: needs reply` | A question or problem report that no maintainer has replied to and that is not resolved. |

Remove a status label from any discussion that matches the first row.

### Type (exactly one)

| Label | When |
| --- | --- |
| `new test` | The PR adds at least one new check (a new `tests/**/Test.<ID>.ps1`), or the issue or idea asks for one. A PR that also fixes other things is still `new test`. |
| `bug` | Fixes, or reports, behaviour that is wrong. A check with the wrong result (false pass or false fail) is a `bug`. |
| `enhancement` | A new capability or an improvement to an existing one that is not a new check, including changes to a check's attributes (severity, product, ResourceType and so on). |
| `documentation` | Only docs or the website's content change, or the issue is about docs. |
| `maintenance` | Refactoring, build, CI, dependency or repository housekeeping with no user-visible change. |
| `question` | An issue or discussion asking how to use Maester. Not for PRs. |

Conventional-commit prefixes in a PR title are a hint (`feat` → `enhancement` or `new test`,
`fix` → `bug`, `docs` → `documentation`, `chore`/`ci`/`build`/`refactor` → `maintenance`), but
the diff decides.

### Product (zero to three)

Use the product keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`: `product: entra`,
`exchange`, `defender`, `intune`, `purview`, `sharepoint`, `teams`, `microsoft-365`, `azure`,
`azure-devops`, `github`, `ad`, `copilot-studio`. For a PR that adds or changes checks, count the
`Product` of each check it touches and keep the three products with the most checks, dropping
any product with a single check when the PR touches more than three products. For an issue or
discussion, the product the report is about. Engine changes that are not specific to one service
get no product.

### Suite (zero or more)

A proposal for a new benchmark gets no suite label until that suite exists; mention it in the
report so a maintainer can add one to `.github/labels.json`.

`suite: cis`, `suite: cisa`, `suite: eidsca`, `suite: orca`: the PR adds or changes checks in
`tests/<suite>/**` or changes that suite's generator under `build/<suite>/**`, or the item is
about that benchmark's mapping, content or permissions. A one-line attribute alignment in
another suite's check does not add that suite. The MT checks under `tests/maester/**` and the AD
checks under `tests/ad/**` have no suite label; `product:` already covers them.

### Flags (add when true; remove only the ones you can compute)

| Label | When | Who sets it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `needs rebase` | `mergeable` is `CONFLICTING`. Remove it when the conflict is gone. | Triage |
| `generated` | Every changed file is generated, as in the bot PRs that regenerate test docs. Generated files are `website/docs/tests/**`, `website/versioned_docs/**`, `**/fixtures/golden/**`, `website/src/data/test-builder.json`, `packs/*/catalog.json`, the upstream-generated suites `tests/eidsca/**`, `tests/orca/**` and `powershell/internal/generated/**`, the agent and skill copies `.claude/agents/**`, `.claude/skills/**` and `website/docs/agents-and-skills.md` that `build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1` writes, `*.dll`, lock files, and any other file whose first lines contain both "Generated by" and "Do not edit". | Triage |
| `breaking change` | It removes or renames a public cmdlet, parameter, output field or test ID, changes a default, removes a check from the default run, or changes what a check considers correct. Fixing a check so that it matches its documented behaviour is a `bug`, not a breaking change. On an issue: the request or the reported fix would need such a change. | Triage adds; only a maintainer removes |
| `attribute-review-override`, `good first issue`, `help wanted` | Maintainer judgement. | Never set or remove |

### Resolution (maintainers only)

`duplicate`, `superseded`, `wontfix` and `invalid` explain why something was closed. Triage
never sets or removes them; it suggests them in the report.

## Checks before you report

- Every open PR and issue you touched has exactly one `status:` and one type label.
- No label you added is missing from `.github/labels.json`.
- For each `status: changes requested`, you can name the maintainer review or comment, and you
  checked that no author commit came after it.
- A maintainer's approval followed by a later maintainer ask is not an approval.
- For each `status: needs decision`, you can state the open question in one line.

# Microsoft Entra B2B integration for SharePoint & OneDrive - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

Important

Between May and July 2026, Microsoft enabled SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Microsoft Entra B2B for new external sharing in commercial tenants. The `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` setting no longer controls sharing behavior for these tenants, and the integration can't be disabled.

Starting in October 2026, Microsoft will retire SharePoint Online one-time passcode (OTP) authentication for commercial tenants. Microsoft Entra B2B email one-time passcode authentication remains supported.

When SharePoint OTP retirement reaches your tenant, external users need a matching Microsoft Entra B2B guest account in your directory to access previously shared **Specific people** links. Users with a matching guest account retain access. If a guest account is missing, an administrator can create one, or a user with sharing permissions can share or reshare at least one file, folder, or site to create it and restore access to previously shared content.

For more information, see [FAQ on improvements to external sharing in OneDrive and SharePoint](faqs-odspintegrationwithentrab2b).

This article describes how to enable Microsoft SharePoint and Microsoft OneDrive integration with [Microsoft Entra B2B](/en-us/entra/external-id/what-is-b2b).

Microsoft Entra B2B provides authentication and management of guests. When enabled, [email one-time passcode](/en-us/entra/external-id/one-time-passcode) is a fallback for guests who can't sign in through another supported authentication method.

When you integrate SharePoint and OneDrive with Microsoft Entra B2B Invitation Manager, you can share files, folders, list items, document libraries, and sites with external people. This feature provides an upgraded experience from the existing secure external sharing recipient experience. Additionally, Microsoft Entra B2B Invitation Manager offers a one-time passcode feature. This feature allows users without work, school, or Microsoft accounts to authenticate by using a code, instead of creating a new account.

Enabling this integration doesn't change your sharing settings. For example, if you have site collections where external sharing is turned off, it remains off.

SharePoint and OneDrive integration with the Microsoft Entra B2B one-time passcode feature is enabled by default for new tenants.

Advantages of Microsoft Entra B2B include:

- Invited people outside your organization each get an account in the directory and are subject to Microsoft Entra ID access policies such as multifactor authentication.
- Invitations to a SharePoint site use Microsoft Entra B2B and no longer require users to have or create a Microsoft account.
- If you have Google federation in Microsoft Entra ID, federated users can now access SharePoint and OneDrive resources that you shared with them.
- SharePoint and OneDrive sharing is subject to the Microsoft Entra organizational relationships settings, such as **Members can invite** and **Guests can invite**. As with Microsoft 365 Groups and Teams, if a Microsoft Entra organizational relationship setting is more restrictive than a SharePoint or OneDrive setting, the Microsoft Entra setting prevails.

Note

Microsoft Entra B2B doesn't support Microsoft accounts in Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet.

## Enabling the integration

For commercial tenants, Microsoft Entra B2B integration is already enabled for new external sharing. You don't need to run the command below. The following procedure applies only to tenants where the `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` setting still controls the integration.

Note

When you enable the integration, people outside the organization are invited through the Azure B2B platform when sharing from SharePoint. They sign in based on the [Microsoft Entra B2B redemption policy](/en-us/azure/active-directory/external-identities/redemption-experience#invitation-redemption-flow). When you don't enable the integration, people outside the organization continue to use their existing accounts created when previously invited to the tenant. Any sharing to new people outside the organization may result in either Microsoft Entra ID-backed accounts or SharePoint-only email auth guests that use a SharePoint One Time Passcode experience to sign in.

To enable SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Microsoft Entra B2B

1. [Download the latest SharePoint Online Management Shell](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=255251).
2. Connect to SharePoint with permissions of a [SharePoint Administrator](/en-us/sharepoint/sharepoint-admin-role) or [more](/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/add-users/about-admin-roles) in Microsoft 365. To learn how, see [Getting started with SharePoint Online Management Shell](/en-us/powershell/sharepoint/sharepoint-online/connect-sharepoint-online).
3. Run the following cmdlets:

    ```PowerShell
    Set-SPOTenant -EnableAzureADB2BIntegration $true
    ```

Note

Review any custom [domain sharing restrictions in SharePoint and OneDrive](/en-us/sharepoint/restricted-domains-sharing) and decide if they should be moved to the [Microsoft Entra B2B Allow/Deny list](/en-us/azure/active-directory/external-identities/allow-deny-list). The Microsoft Entra ID Allow/Deny list also affects other Microsoft 365 services like Teams and Microsoft 365 Groups.

## Disabling the integration

Microsoft Entra B2B integration can't be disabled in commercial tenants. The following procedure applies only to tenants where the `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` setting still controls the integration.

You can disable the integration by running [`Set-SPOTenant`](/en-us/powershell/module/sharepoint-online/Set-SPOTenant)`-EnableAzureADB2BIntegration $false`.

Important

When you disable the integration, previously shared users remain Microsoft Entra Guest Users for future shares. To convert a user from a Microsoft Entra Guest User back to a SharePoint OTP user, you need to [delete the guest](/en-us/sharepoint/remove-users#delete-a-guest-from-the-microsoft-365-admin-center) in Microsoft Entra ID and remove all SPUser objects in your organization that reference that guest user.

## Frequently asked questions

The following questions address SharePoint OTP retirement and access to content shared with external users.

**1. How can I check if my tenant has enabled SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Entra B2B?**

**Answer:** In commercial tenants, integration is already enabled for new external sharing, regardless of the `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` value. For tenants where the setting still controls the integration, run `Get-SPOTenant` in the SharePoint Online Management Shell and check the `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` property. A value of `True` means the integration is enabled; `False` means it isn't enabled.

**2. Which tenants are affected by the October 2026 SharePoint OTP retirement?**

**Answer:** The October 2026 retirement applies to commercial tenants. It affects external users who access previously shared **Specific people** links through SharePoint OTP and don't have a matching Microsoft Entra B2B guest account in your directory.

**3. What happens to previously shared links when SharePoint OTP is retired?**

**Answer:** External users with a matching Microsoft Entra B2B guest account retain access to previously shared links. Once retirement reaches your commercial tenant during October 2026, users without a matching guest account receive access denied on previously shared **Specific people** links. To restore access, create a guest account matching the email address used for the original sharing link, or share or reshare at least one file, folder, or site with that user. You don't need to reshare each item individually.

**4. Is there a way to report which previously shared links and external users are affected?**

**Answer:** Yes. You can use audit logs to assess the impact. For more information, see [Use sharing auditing in the audit log](/en-us/purview/audit-log-sharing?tabs=microsoft-purview-portal). Additionally, site sharing reports available through Microsoft Graph Data Connect can help identify affected content and users. Details are provided in the [Microsoft Graph Data Connect for SharePoint Blog](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft_graph_data_connect_for_sharepo/mgdc-for-sharepoint-faq-what-is-in-the-permissions-dataset/4075447). You can also report on file and folder sharing in a SharePoint site using [this sharing report](/en-us/sharepoint/sharing-reports?WT.mc_id=M365-MVP-9501).

**5. Can I proactively invite existing users to join via Entra B2B before this change takes effect?**

**Answer:** Yes. You can create a Microsoft Entra B2B guest account in advance using the email address associated with the original sharing link. A matching guest account lets the user retain access to previously shared content without resharing. For more information, see [Add and manage B2B collaboration users](/en-us/entra/external-id/add-users-administrator).

**6. Can exceptions be made to this change?**

**Answer:** No. This update is part of Microsoft's ongoing efforts to enhance security.

**7. Can this change be applied at the site level?**

**Answer:** No. The change applies at the tenant level and can't be scoped to individual sites.

result.output:
**Exact retirement date:** May 1, 2026. After that date, legacy client authentication is "permanently blocked and cannot be re-enabled." The message also says legacy auth was blocked by default starting February 16, 2026.

**Re-enablement:** Only temporarily. Organizations could re-enable it using PowerShell until April 30, 2026. After May 1, 2026, it cannot be turned back on.

**Relation to LegacyAuthProtocolsEnabled:** Yes. The message says to set `AllowLegacyAuthProtocolsEnabledSetting` and `LegacyAuthProtocolsEnabled` to TRUE to allow legacy authentication temporarily, until April 30, 2026. It links to the Set-SPOTenant documentation for the `-LegacyAuthProtocolsEnabled` parameter.

content.text:
I've applied the labels to all 7 PRs, and each now has exactly one status and one type.

## Review of [#2590](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2590): CIS 7.2.x SharePoint guides

**What it does:** It updates the guides for seven SharePoint sharing checks (CIS 7.2.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.6, 7.2.7, 7.2.8 and 7.2.10) to cover the 2026 service changes. It only changes the `.md` guides, not the checks' code.

**The service-change details are right.** I checked them against Microsoft's [Entra B2B integration page](https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/sharepoint-azureb2b-integration) (updated 7 Oct 2026) and the Message center post MC1184649:
- Entra B2B integration was switched on for commercial tenants between May and July 2026. `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` no longer controls it, and it can't be turned off.
- SharePoint one-time passcodes are being retired from October 2026, while Entra B2B email passcodes still work. Existing "Specific people" links stop working for anyone without a matching guest account, and creating that guest account or resharing one item restores access.
- The old IDCRL sign-in protocol was retired on 1 May 2026 and can't be turned back on.
- Microsoft's page says to review SharePoint domain restrictions before moving them to the Entra allow/deny list, and that Entra invite settings take precedence over SharePoint's.

It's also careful to say what each check doesn't verify, which is useful for anyone reading a result.

**What needs fixing:**
1. **Six links include `/en-us/`.** These are in 7.2.10, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.6, 7.2.7 and 7.2.8, and they're the only reason the ubuntu build fails. The fix is to remove `en-us/` from each.
2. **A duplicate link in 7.2.2.** The guide already links to the same page through its "Enabling the integration" link, so the new link isn't needed.
3. **Minor, optional:** four guides start the new paragraph with a bold label (e.g. "**Current service behavior:**") and three don't. I'd leave that as it is.

**Separate from this PR:** the 7.2.2 guide now says that `False` "may not reflect actual B2B behavior" in commercial tenants. That means the check itself will fail tenants where the integration is actually on. Whether it should pass or skip in commercial tenants is a separate decision about how the check behaves, not something for this docs PR.

**Recommendation: fix it ourselves and merge.** It's only docs, so there's nothing that needs testing in a tenant. Both fixes are mechanical, and sending it back would only delay it.
Fix and merge

﻿function Test-MtCisFabricServicePrincipalProfilesRestricted {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that service-principal profiles are disabled or limited to one or more security groups.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Service-principal profiles support multitenant applications. A compromised service principal with profile access could cross customer data boundaries; restricting this setting limits which application identities can use that capability.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CIS.M365.9.1.11',
        Title = 'Restrict service principal profiles in Fabric',
        Product = 'fabric',
        Feature = 'developer-settings',
        Area = 'applications',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
        Control = ('cis-m365:9.1.11', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-3'),
        Service = 'Azure',
        Author = 'JeremyFinney-lgtm'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    return Test-MtCisFabricTenantSetting -SettingName 'AllowServicePrincipalsCreateAndUseProfiles' -SettingTitle 'Allow service principals to create and use profiles' -Rule DisabledOrGroups
}
Service-principal profile creation and use are disabled or limited to one or more security groups.

Profiles are used by multitenant applications to isolate customer contexts. Restricting this capability helps contain misuse of an application identity and protects those boundaries.

#### Remediation action

1. Sign in to [Microsoft Fabric](https://app.fabric.microsoft.com) with a Fabric administrator account.
2. Select **OneLake catalog** > **Govern** > **Configurations** > **Tenant settings**. If these options aren't available in your region, select **Settings** > **Admin portal** > **Tenant settings**.
3. Under **Developer settings**, find **Allow service principals to create and use profiles**.
4. Choose **Disabled**, or choose **Enabled** and scope the setting to **Specific security groups** containing the applications that need this access.
5. Select **Apply**.

#### Related links

* [Developer admin settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/admin/service-admin-portal-developer#allow-service-principals-to-create-and-use-profiles)
* [CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/microsoft_365)

content.text:
## Review of [#2556](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2556): CIS M365 Fabric checks (9.1.1–9.1.12)

**What it does:** It adds 12 CIS checks for Microsoft Fabric tenant settings, such as guest access, publish to web, R and Python visuals, and service principal API access. One helper reads all the tenant settings from the Fabric admin API. It gets a Fabric access token from the Azure connection, follows paging and caches the result. A second helper applies one of four rules to each setting: disabled or limited to groups, publish to web, must be disabled, or must be enabled. It also adds `fabric` to the taxonomy, adds requirements 9.1.1–9.1.12 to the CIS framework file, and includes unit tests for the helper. All checks pass.

**What's good:**
- Each check is a single line that calls the shared helper, so the setting names and rules are easy to compare with the benchmark.
- It reports an error rather than a pass when a setting is missing or has an unexpected value, so a bad response can't look like a pass.
- The settings are read once per run and shared by all 12 checks, and the cache is cleared between runs.
- Each check's rule fits its setting. For example, 9.1.10 requires that "Block ResourceKey Authentication" is on, and 9.1.4 requires that new publish-to-web embed codes are off.

**What needs fixing:**
1. **The Fabric code is in `azure` folders.** The product is `fabric`, and our layout rule says the folder is named after the product whose settings a check reads. The helpers should move to `internal/services/fabric/` and `internal/checks/cis/fabric/`, and `fabric` needs adding to the service list in `website/docs/contributing.md` and in `RepositoryLayout.Tests.ps1`. Keeping `Service = 'Azure'` is fine, because the checks connect through the Azure context.
2. **The PR edits generated docs by hand.** It changes 14 files under `website/docs/tests/**` and `website/src/data/test-builder.json`. Those should be dropped, and the docs bot will regenerate them after merge.
3. **The only conflict with `main` is in a generated file**, `powershell/tests/fixtures/golden/selection.json`. It's rebuilt with `build/golden/Export-MtGoldenFixture.ps1`.
4. **The required permission isn't written anywhere.** The Fabric admin API needs the Fabric Administrator role, or, for a service principal, the Fabric tenant setting that allows service principals to use read-only admin APIs. Nothing in the docs says this, so users will get errors they can't explain.
5. **There's no `product: fabric` label.** It should be added to `.github/labels.json` once the taxonomy key goes in.

**Recommendation: fix it ourselves, then ask Jeremy to retest.** Items 1–3 and 5 are mechanical. Item 4 is a short docs addition. Moving the helpers changes file paths but not logic, but I'd still want Jeremy to rerun the 12 checks on his tenant before we merge.

They're part of the **CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark**, not the Azure benchmark. Fabric is section 9 of that benchmark ("Microsoft Fabric", 9.1.x), and it has been since v3.0. I found no separate CIS benchmark for Fabric or Power BI.

**What I found:**
- **Tenable** has copies of the M365 benchmark's audit files for v3.1.0 and v5.0.0. These list the Fabric recommendations under 9.1.x with the same numbers this PR uses: 9.1.1 guest user access, 9.1.2 external invitations, 9.1.3 guest access to content, 9.1.4 publish to web, 9.1.10 service principal API access, and 9.1.11 service principal profiles.
- **CIS's own CIS-CAT documentation** says the M365 benchmark covers Power BI (Fabric) along with Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Entra ID.
- **No standalone Fabric benchmark showed up.** The only "Power BI CIS" result was Prowler's dashboard for viewing CIS results, which isn't a benchmark.

**What this means for #2556:**
- Mapping the checks as `cis-m365:9.1.x` and putting them in `tests/cis` is correct.
- Adding requirements 9.1.1–9.1.12 to `cis-m365.json` is correct.
- The folder fix from my review still applies. The benchmark is M365, but the checks read Fabric settings, and the layout rule names folders after the product: `internal/services/fabric/`, not `azure/`.

- I couldn't open the CIS benchmark itself, which needs a CIS WorkBench login. These sources are third-party copies plus CIS's tool documentation.

<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Regenerates the Maester 2.x golden fixtures (tags and blocks, selection, config layouts).

    .DESCRIPTION
    Freezes today's (2.x) behaviour so later Maester 3.0 milestones can prove parity
    (design: docs/proposals/maester-3.0-design.md, sections 4, 7 and 15.2).

    Nothing here needs a tenant and no test body is executed:

    tags-and-blocks.json
        Every It in tests/**/*.Tests.ps1 (tests/Custom excluded), found by Pester discovery
        (Run.SkipRun = $true). For each It: Id, Name, Block, SelectionTags, ResultTags, File, Line.
          - Id and Block are computed exactly as ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult does (Id: text before the
            first colon after stripping the 'See https' suffix; Block: $test.Block.ExpandedName).
          - SelectionTags: the tags Pester filters on (tags of every ancestor Describe/Context plus the
            It tags), de-duplicated and sorted case-insensitively.
          - ResultTags: the Tag array ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult writes today,
            @($test.Block.Tag + $test.Tag | Select-Object -Unique). Only the immediate parent block's
            tags are included, so tests nested in a Context lose their Describe tags.
        A native test (every built-in test in 3.0) has one entry from the catalog: SelectionTags are the
        tags -Tag matches (the tags it carries, its ID and its 2.x tags from Maester.LegacyTags.json),
        ResultTags the tags its author wrote, and Block the name of its product. The committed file is
        the frozen 2.x snapshot; the golden test checks that every tag in it still selects the same tests.
        Its whose name is built at run time (an expandable string or a '<template>') are families
        (MT.1024, MT.1033, MT.1034, MT.1059, MT1060). They are recorded once, by literal ID prefix,
        with "Family": true, from the AST. Discovery-time tenant calls are neutralised by a stub
        module; any file whose discovery still fails falls back to an AST scan and is listed in _meta.

    selection.json
        For a list of Invoke-Maester command lines, the Pester filter Invoke-Maester builds and the IDs
        it selects. The filter is captured from the real Invoke-Maester code path: Invoke-Pester is
        shadowed inside the Maester module scope so the configuration is captured instead of run.
        The captured filter is then applied by a real Pester discovery of the built-in tests. Family
        entries (invisible to discovery without a tenant) are selected with a replica of Pester's tag
        filter, which is verified against Pester's own result for every discovered test.

    config-layouts/<layout>/expected.json
        For each committed layout folder, the config file(s) the real 2.x Get-MtMaesterConfig picks
        and the effective GlobalSettings and Severity for a few IDs, with and without a tenant ID.

content.text:
The false failure is in [`Test.CIS.M365.7.2.2.ps1`](tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.7.2.2.ps1). It passes only when `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` is `True`. In commercial tenants, Microsoft turned the integration on for everyone between May and July 2026, and the property no longer controls it. So a commercial tenant whose property still reads `False` (the default) fails, even though the integration is on and can't be turned off. Before #2590 the guide even told people to run `Set-SPOTenant`, and now that does nothing. This false failure isn't something #2590 introduced. #2590 only documents it.

## Proposed fix

Decide the result by cloud as well as by the property:

| Tenant | Property | Result | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any | `True` | Pass | Unchanged |
| Commercial | `False` | **Pass** | "Microsoft turned on Entra B2B integration for new external sharing in commercial tenants between May and July 2026, and it can't be turned off. `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` reads False but no longer controls it." |
| GCC High, DoD, China, other sovereign clouds | `False` | Fail | Unchanged: there the property still controls the integration |
| Cloud unknown | `False` | Fail | Unchanged, as the safe default |

The engine already works out the tenant's cloud for its `Cloud` gate, in [`Read-MtTenantContext.ps1`](powershell/internal/connect/Read-MtTenantContext.ps1:106). It reads the Graph environment: `Global` → Commercial, `USGov` → GCC High, `USGovDoD` → DoD, `China` → China. The check would read that value instead of working it out again.

**Why pass, not skip:** the CIS requirement is "ensure the integration is enabled", and in commercial tenants it is. A skip would leave the requirement looking unchecked in a CIS report, even though the integration is guaranteed to be on.

**One risk: GCC.** GCC (moderate) uses the worldwide endpoint, so Graph reports it as Commercial. The engine marks that case as `Assumed`. Microsoft's page says the rollout applies to "commercial tenants" and doesn't say whether GCC is included. If GCC is excluded, a GCC tenant with `False` would get a false pass. There are two ways to handle that:
- **Accept it for now.** The pass message would say it's based on the Commercial cloud, and GCC tenants can set `Cloud = 'GCC'` in their config so the check goes back to reading the property.
- **Detect GCC properly.** The tenant's OpenID discovery document (`login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration`) returns `tenant_region_sub_scope: "GCC"` for GCC tenants. Adding that to `Read-MtTenantContext` would let the engine tell GCC apart from Commercial for every check, not just this one. It's a bigger change, and better as its own PR.

**Docs to match:** the 7.2.2 guide that #2590 just changed says a `False` value "may not reflect actual B2B behavior". With this fix that sentence becomes wrong, so it would change to say that commercial tenants pass whatever the property's value.

This is a small change to the check and its guide plus a unit test. I'd do it as its own PR after #2590 merges, and leave GCC detection for later. #2590 still needs either an admin merge or a second maintainer's approval.

Description:
Entra ID B2B provides authentication and management of guests. Authentication
happens via one-time passcode when they don't already have a work or school account
or a Microsoft account. Integration with SharePoint and OneDrive allows for more
granular control of how guest user accounts are managed in the organization's AAD,
unifying a similar guest experience already deployed in other Microsoft 365 services
such as Teams.
Note: Global Reader role currently can't access SharePoint using PowerShell.
Rationale:
External users assigned guest accounts will be subject to Entra ID access policies, such
as multi-factor authentication. This provides a way to manage guest identities and
control access to SharePoint and OneDrive resources. Without this integration, files can
be shared without account registration, making it more challenging to audit and manage
who has access to the organization's data.

CIS v7.0.0 checks the property and nothing else. It says nothing about Microsoft turning the integration on automatically. This is from printed page 466 (page 467 of the PDF):

**7.2.2 Ensure SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Azure AD B2B is enabled (Automated)**. Profile: E3 Level 1 and E5 Level 1.

**Audit:**
```powershell
Connect-SPOService
Get-SPOTenant | ft EnableAzureADB2BIntegration
```
> 3. Verify that the returned value is True.

**Remediation:**
```powershell
Set-SPOTenant -EnableAzureADB2BIntegration $true
```

**Default value:** False.

**What CIS cites and says about impact:** the references include Microsoft's B2B integration page, at its `#enabling-the-integration` section. The Impact section only warns that existing one-time-passcode links break after you enable the integration.

## What this means for the fix

Our check, [`Test.CIS.M365.7.2.2.ps1`](tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.7.2.2.ps1), does exactly what CIS's audit says: it passes only when `EnableAzureADB2BIntegration` is `True`. So the failure in commercial tenants isn't a bug in our check. The benchmark is behind the service. CIS published v7.0.0 around July 2026 (your copy is dated 9 July), while Microsoft was still rolling the change out, and the benchmark doesn't mention it.

That makes the pass-in-commercial idea I proposed a choice rather than a fix. You'd be choosing between:

- **Follow CIS exactly (no code change).** Commercial tenants with `False` keep failing, which matches CIS's own audit and any CIS-CAT result. The 7.2.2 guide from #2590 already explains that the failure doesn't mean the integration is off. I'd tighten that sentence to say so outright: in commercial tenants this fails by CIS's audit even though Microsoft has turned the integration on. The remediation should also say that running `Set-SPOTenant` there does nothing.
- **Follow what CIS is trying to achieve.** Commercial tenants pass with the explanation, as I proposed. This is more accurate about the tenant's security, but Maester's 7.2.2 result would then differ from CIS's audit. Anyone comparing the two would see different results, and we'd carry that difference until CIS updates the benchmark.

I'd lean towards the first: keep the check matching CIS's audit, and make the guide say clearly that this failure is expected. A CIS-numbered check should give the result CIS's audit gives. We can change it when CIS updates 7.2.2 in the next version.

The Copilot Studio security tests (MT.1113–MT.1122) use the Dataverse OData API via `Az.Accounts`. Authenticate with `Connect-AzAccount` and then connect Maester for Copilot Studio access.

```powershell
# Authenticate to Az (SPN example)
```

### Microsoft Fabric (via Az.Accounts)

The CIS Microsoft Fabric checks (CIS.M365.9.1.1–9.1.12) read the tenant settings from the [Fabric admin API](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/fabric/admin/tenants/list-tenant-settings) with a token from your Azure context. Connect with `Connect-AzAccount` (or `Connect-Maester -Service Azure`) before running `Invoke-Maester`.

```powershell
# Interactive, as a Fabric administrator
Connect-AzAccount

# Non-interactive (service principal)
Connect-AzAccount -ServicePrincipal -ApplicationId $applicationId -TenantId $tenantId -CertificatePath /cert.pfx
```

> A user must hold the **Fabric Administrator** role. A service principal or managed identity must be allowed to call the admin APIs: in the Fabric admin portal, under **Admin API settings**, turn on **Service principals can access read-only admin APIs** and add a security group that contains the service principal. Without this access the API returns 403 and the Fabric checks are reported as not authorized.

Users need the Fabric Administrator role. A service principal needs **Service principals can access read-only admin APIs** turned on for a security group that contains it. Without that access, the checks report an error. Maester doesn't turn a 403 into "not authorized" for these checks automatically.
- **Label:** `product: fabric` is now in `labels.json` and the triage skill's product list. It isn't on GitHub yet, because `Sync-GitHubLabels.ps1 -Apply` has to run after the merge.

**Unit tests:** 4,194 of 4,196 pass. Of the two failures, one is the ZTA test that fails on `main` too. The other was the `test-builder.json` check, which passes now that the file is back.

**How the commits are laid out:** a clean merge with the latest `main`, followed by one fix commit. A chained git command went wrong partway through and committed early. Nothing had been pushed, so I rebuilt the branch from Jeremy's original commit, and nothing was lost.

The comment is drafted in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill-github-maester/cad13d5b-f6a5-465e-ab70-f69ded04259c/scratchpad/comment-2556.md`. "The author pushed" includes co-authors and agents committing for the author. When the PR's
author is a maintainer, their own pushes count the same way. A merge commit from `main` on its
own is not a response; look for a commit that changes the files the review was about.

Issues. Take the first rule that matches.

| Label | When |
| --- | --- |
| `status: awaiting confirmation` | A PR that closes it has merged, or a maintainer said the fix shipped and is waiting for the reporter. Suggest closing it in the report. |
| `status: blocked` | It waits on another open item, an unreleased feature, or an upstream product or module fix. |
| `status: needs info` | A maintainer's latest comment asks the reporter a question and the reporter has not answered. |
| `status: needs decision` | A maintainer has to decide whether or how to do it, including a reporter asking a maintainer to choose (a severity, a default, an approach). |
| `status: in progress` | An open PR closes it (a closing keyword such as "fixes #N", or the Development sidebar), or it has an assignee and activity in the last 90 days. A mention such as "related to #N" or "tracked in #N" does not count. |
| `status: accepted` | A maintainer opened it, labelled it, confirmed the bug or agreed to the feature, and nobody has started it. |
| `status: needs triage` | No maintainer has engaged yet, **or** the reporter answered a maintainer's question and it is the maintainers' turn again. |

A maintainer opening, labelling or assigning an issue counts as engaging with it. Skip pinned
issues (such as the MT test ID reservation thread, #697): they are permanent and take no status.

Discussions. Take the first rule that matches; a discussion that matches none gets no status.

# Manage Azure subscription policies - Microsoft Cost Management | Microsoft Learn

This article helps you to configure Azure subscription policies to control the movement of Azure subscriptions from and into directories. The default behavior of these two policies is set to **Allow no users (recommended)** to help protect tenants from unauthorized subscription transfers. Global administrators can change these settings to **Allow all users** if needed. Note that the setting of **Allow all users** allows all authorized users, including authorized guest users on a subscription, to be able to transfer them. It does not mean all users in a directory.

Important

To improve tenant security, on May 1st, 2026, Microsoft updated the default behavior for subscription transfer policies. Subscriptions can no longer be transferred in to or out of your directory unless a global administrator explicitly allows it.

If your organization previously set an explicit policy, that choice continues to be respected — no action is needed.

If your organization never configured these policies and your workflows rely on users being able to move subscriptions in or out of your tenant, **those workflows will break as a result of this change**. To restore the previous behavior, a global administrator can update either policy to **Allow all users**.

## Prerequisites

- Only directory [global administrators](../../active-directory/roles/permissions-reference#global-administrator) with direct role assignment can edit subscription policies. Before editing subscription policies, the global administrator must [Elevate access to manage all Azure subscriptions and management groups](../../role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin). Then they can edit subscription policies.
- All other users can only read the current policy setting.
- Subscriptions transferred into or out of a directory must remain associated with a Billing Tenant to ensure billing occurs correctly.

## Available subscription policy settings

Use the following policy settings to control the movement of Azure subscriptions from and into directories.

### Subscriptions leaving a Microsoft Entra ID directory

The policy allows or stops users from moving subscriptions out of the current directory. Subscription owners can transfer subscriptions to another directory where they're a member, using either the Azure portal or APIs. Global administrators use this setting to allow or block these transfers for all directory users. This policy applies to all authorized users, including authorized guest users in your directory.

- **Allow no users (recommended)** — Blocks all subscription transfers out of your directory. This is the default.
- **Allow all users** — Permits authorized users to transfer subscriptions out of your directory.

### Subscriptions entering a Microsoft Entra ID directory

This policy controls whether users from other directories can move subscriptions into your directory. Subscription owners who are members of your directory can transfer subscriptions in using the Azure portal or APIs. Global administrators use this setting to allow or block these transfers. This policy applies to all authorized users, including authorized guest users in your directory.

- **Allow no users (recommended)** — Blocks all subscription transfers into your directory. This is the default.
- **Allow all users** — Permits authorized users to transfer subscriptions into your directory.

### Exempted Users

For governance reasons, global administrators can block all subscription directory moves - in to or out of the current directory. However they might want to allow specific users to do both operations. For both situations, they can configure a list of exempted users that allows these users to bypass all the policy settings that apply to everyone else.

#### Important note

Authorized users (including guest users) in your directory can create Azure subscriptions in another directory where they have billing permissions and then transfer those subscriptions into your Entra ID directory. The default policy settings (**Allow no users**) help protect against this scenario. If your organization has changed either policy to **Allow all users**, be aware of this risk and consider reverting to the recommended default:

- Subscriptions leaving Entra ID directory should be set to **Allow no users (recommended)**.
- Subscriptions entering Entra ID directory should be set to **Allow no users (recommended)**.

## Setting subscription policy

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
2. Navigate to **Subscriptions**. **Manage Policies** is shown on the command bar. [![Screenshot of the Azure Subscriptions blade with the Manage Policies button highlighted.](media/manage-azure-subscription-policy/subscription-blade-manage-policies.png)](media/manage-azure-subscription-policy/subscription-blade-manage-policies.png#lightbox)
3. Select **Manage Policies** to view details about the current subscription policies set for the directory. A global administrator with [elevated permissions](../../role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin) can make edits to the settings including adding or removing exempted users.[![Screenshot of the Manage Policies pane showing subscription policy details.](media/manage-azure-subscription-policy/2026-04-15-14-52-13.png)](media/manage-azure-subscription-policy/2026-04-15-14-52-13.png#lightbox)
4. Select **Save changes** at the bottom to save changes. The changes are effective immediately.

## Read subscription policy

Non-global administrators can still navigate to the subscription policy area to view the directory's policy settings. They can't make any edits. They can't see the list of exempted users for privacy reasons. They can view their global administrators to submit requests for policy changes, as long as the directory settings allow them to.

**One of your review points was wrong.** Point 3 said Microsoft's default is "Allow everyone". [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/manage-azure-subscription-policy) says that on 1 May 2026 the default became **"Allow no users"**, which blocks transfers. So the `.md` sentence that the block is on by default is correct.

That raises a question about the `TenantPolicyNotFound` branch. If a tenant that never set a policy gets that response, its transfers are blocked by default, yet the test reports a fail. Oppedijk says Microsoft now returns a default policy, so this branch may never run. Either way, I'd make it pass with a note rather than fail.

It isn't in the CIS **Microsoft 365** benchmark. Your v7.0.0 PDF doesn't mention the subscription transfer policy anywhere.

It is in the CIS **Azure** Foundations benchmark (sources: [Tenable v4.0.0 audit](https://www.tenable.com/audits/items/CIS_Microsoft_Azure_Foundations_v4.0.0_L2.audit:1d8f72558170c6d5638e34d6e6c2f6f8), [Turbot CIS v5.0 5.25](https://hub.guardrails.turbot.com/mods/azure/controls/azure-cisv5-0/r0525)):

| --- | --- |
| v3.0.0 | 2.25 (Level 2) |
| v4.0.0 | 6.25 (Level 2) |
| v5.0.0 | 5.25 (Identity Services, Level 2) |

All three word it as "Ensure that 'Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant' **and** 'Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant' is set to 'Permit no one'".

For #2472, that means:
- **MT.1227 is the right ID.** Maester has no CIS Azure framework file (only `cis-m365` and `cis-github`), so there's no `cis-azure:5.25` for the check to map to. It belongs in `tests/maester/azure/` as an MT check, as Oppedijk wrote it.
- **It covers only half the CIS control.** It checks `blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant`. CIS also requires `blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant`, which comes back in the same policy response. Microsoft's Learn page also recommends blocking both directions, because an insider can create a subscription in a tenant they control and move it in. If we fix this ourselves, I'd add that check too, as a second test or as part of this one.
- **The CIS text is out of date.** It says the default is "Allow everyone". Microsoft changed it to "Allow no users" on 1 May 2026, which is probably where your 22 Oct review point came from.

`CIS_Microsoft_Azure_Foundations_Benchmark_v6.0.0.pdf` is in Downloads; its cover says "V6.0.0 - 04-19-2026". In v6.0.0 the control has moved to **5.6** (it was 5.25 in v5.0.0). It's on printed pages 111–112.

**5.6: Ensure that 'Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant' and 'Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant' is set to 'Permit no one'** (Level 2, Manual)
- **Audit:** in the Azure portal, open Subscriptions, then Manage Policies, and check that both settings are "Permit no one".
- **Remediation:** set both settings to "Permit no one" in the same place, then save.
- **Default value:** CIS still says both are "Allow everyone (default)". That's out of date: Microsoft changed the default to "Allow no users" on 1 May 2026, a couple of weeks after this release.
- **References:** the Microsoft Learn subscription policy page, "How subscriptions are associated with a directory", and MCSB IM-2.

What this means for #2472:
- **It checks only half the control.** The recommendation covers both directions, but MT.1227 only checks `blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant`. `blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant` comes back in the same API response, so adding it is a few lines.
- **It stays an MT test.** Maester has no `cis-azure` framework file, so there's nothing to map 5.6 to. The test can say in its Markdown that it lines up with CIS Azure 5.6.

function Test-MtSubscriptionTransferBlocked {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks whether Azure subscriptions are blocked from leaving and entering the tenant.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Checks the tenant-level Azure subscription policy. Allowing subscriptions to leave
    the tenant can let a privileged user transfer their resources to an external tenant.
    Allowing subscriptions to enter the tenant can let a user bring in a subscription
    they control from another tenant.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MT.1227',
        Title              = 'Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving and entering the tenant',
        Product            = 'azure',
        Feature            = 'subscriptions',
        Area               = 'infrastructure',
        ResourceType       = 'Tenant',
        Severity           = 'Medium',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = 'T1537',
        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-4',
        Service            = 'Azure',
        Author             = 'Oppedijk',
        Contributor        = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $policy = Get-MtAzureSubscriptionPolicy

    if ($null -eq $policy) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotAuthorized
        return $null
    }

    $policyNotFound = $policy.code -eq 'TenantPolicyNotFound' -or
        $policy.error.code -eq 'TenantPolicyNotFound'

    if ($policyNotFound) {
        # Since 1 May 2026 a tenant without an explicit policy blocks transfers in both directions.
        $testResultMarkdown = 'Well done. No tenant subscription policy is set, so the Microsoft default blocks subscriptions from leaving and entering the tenant.'
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
        return $true
    }

    if ($policy.error) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error -SkippedError $policy.error.message
        return $null
    }

    $blockLeaving = $policy.properties.blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant -eq $true
    $blockEntering = $policy.properties.blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant -eq $true
    $testResult = $blockLeaving -and $blockEntering

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = 'Well done. The tenant subscription policy blocks subscriptions from leaving and entering the tenant.'
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The tenant subscription policy allows subscriptions to move into or out of the tenant.`n`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Setting | Value |`n| --- | --- |`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant | $(if ($blockLeaving) { 'Permit no one ✅' } else { 'Allow everyone ❌' }) |`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant | $(if ($blockEntering) { 'Permit no one ✅' } else { 'Allow everyone ❌' }) |"
    }

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving and entering the tenant.

The tenant subscription policy controls whether subscription owners can move a subscription out of the tenant or bring one in from another tenant. Allowing subscriptions to leave can let a privileged user transfer a subscription and its resources to an external tenant. Allowing subscriptions to enter can let a user bring in a subscription they control, together with its resources and role assignments.

Since 1 May 2026 Microsoft blocks both directions by default for tenants that never set a policy. A tenant that set **Allow everyone** before then keeps that setting. This check also covers CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v6.0.0 recommendation 5.6.

#### Remediation action

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com) as a Global Administrator with a direct role assignment, and [elevate access](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin) to manage all Azure subscriptions. Other users can read the policy but not change it.
2. Go to **Subscriptions** and select **Manage Policies**.
3. Set **Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant** and **Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant** to **Permit no one**.
4. If specific users must still move subscriptions, add them to **Exempted Users**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

#### Related links

- [Manage Azure subscription policies - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/manage-azure-subscription-policy)
- [Azure portal - Subscriptions](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Billing/SubscriptionsBladeV2)

Thanks @Oppedijk. I've pushed the fixes from my review to your branch, plus a correction to my own review:

- **Microsoft's default has changed.** In point 3 I said the default is "Allow everyone". That was true until 1 May 2026, when Microsoft [changed it to "Allow no users"](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/manage-azure-subscription-policy) for tenants that never set a policy. So your sentence about the default was right. A `TenantPolicyNotFound` response now passes, with a note that the default blocks transfers.
- **The check covers both directions.** CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations v6.0.0 recommendation 5.6 asks for both "Subscription leaving" and "Subscription entering" to be set to "Permit no one", and Microsoft recommends the same. `blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant` comes back in the same response, so the check now requires both. The title is now "Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving and entering the tenant", and the function is renamed to `Test-MtSubscriptionTransferBlocked`. When the check fails, the result shows a table with both settings.
- **An unreadable policy is skipped.** `Invoke-MtAzureRequest` now returns `$null` on 401/403, and that case is skipped as `NotAuthorized` instead of failing. Any other error response is skipped as `Error`.
- **Attributes.** I kept your `subscriptions` feature. `Area` is now `infrastructure`, because the rubric lists subscriptions there. `Control` is now AC-4.
- **Docs.** The remediation now names the right role: a directly assigned Global Administrator who has elevated access, since other users can only read the policy. It uses the portal's Manage Policies steps instead of a PUT, because a PUT also replaces the exempted users. I removed `en-us` from the links.
- **CI.** I added the final newlines, regenerated `selection.json` and `test-builder.json`, and merged `main`.

If you can, please run it once against your tenant before we merge:

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -TestId 'MT.1227'
```

I've pushed the #2472 fixes to Oppedijk's branch (`02b72f7b7`, on top of a merge with the latest `main`) and assigned the PR to Oppedijk. CI is running on the new commit.

**What changed in MT.1227:**
- **It checks both directions.** The check now requires `blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant` as well as `blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant`, which matches CIS Azure v6.0.0 recommendation 5.6. I renamed the function to `Test-MtSubscriptionTransferBlocked` and changed the title to "…leaving and entering the tenant". When it fails, the result shows a table with both settings.
- **What each policy response gives:**

  | Response | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | Both directions blocked | Pass |
  | Either direction allowed | Fail |
  | `TenantPolicyNotFound` | Pass, with a note that Microsoft's default blocks both directions |
  | `$null` (401/403) | Skipped: `NotAuthorized` |
  | Any other error | Skipped: `Error` |

  I checked all five with mocked policy responses.
- **Attributes:** I kept the `subscriptions` feature and changed `Area` to `infrastructure` and `Control` to `nist-800-53-r5:AC-4`.
- **Docs:**
  - The remediation now says you need a directly assigned Global Administrator with elevated access.
  - It walks through the portal's Manage Policies steps instead of a PUT request, and mentions exempted users.
  - The links no longer include `en-us`.
- **CI fixes:** I added the missing final newline, regenerated `selection.json` (each count goes up by 1) and `test-builder.json`, and reverted the macOS case-only fixture change.

**Unit tests:** 4,178 of 4,179 pass. The one failure is the ZTA test that also fails on `main`.

The comment for Oppedijk is in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill-github-maester/cad13d5b-f6a5-465e-ab70-f69ded04259c/scratchpad/comment-2472.md`. It corrects the default from point 3 of your review, lists the changes, and asks Oppedijk to run `Invoke-Maester -TestId 'MT.1227'` against their tenant. Merging this one will also need an admin merge or another maintainer's approval, because you pushed the last commit.
Post it

content.text:
I posted the retest comment on [#2472](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2472#issuecomment-6468669062).

[#2410](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2410) is Jeremy's 23 CIS Exchange, Defender and Purview checks. His commits from 23–24 Oct fixed almost all of your 22 Oct review and Copilot's findings, and CI is green on all three platforms.

**Fixed:**
- 2.1.10 now skips when *any* domain can't be checked, the same as 2.1.8.
- The DMARC, SPF and DKIM parsers now report "no record" (`DNS_INFO_NO_RECORDS`) and a bad record differently from a DNS outage.
- 6.2.1 is fixed on three counts:
  - aliases are resolved before deciding whether a target is external;
  - only enabled outbound policies are checked;
  - it no longer flags `BlindCopyTo`, `CopyTo` and `AddToRecipients`.
- 3.2.1 now has the `EXCHANGE_DLP` licence gate.
- 6.1.2 skips when there are no mailboxes.
- 2.4.2 still requires an explicit recipient condition, because the CIS audit asks for that. Its result now explains why an organisation-wide scope fails.
- 3.2.3 was rewritten and no longer reads `ImmutableIdentity`.
- Attributes:
  - 6.5.1 and MT.1044 are both Low.
  - 6.1.1 is High.
  - 2.1.14 is High, matching ORCA.118.1, which is the option I leaned towards.
  - 3.2.3 matches MT.1175.

**Still open:**
1. **Merge conflicts.** `main` has moved again, and the PR conflicts in `selection.json` and `contributors.json`. Both are mechanical to resolve.
2. **One cross-suite mismatch.** 6.3.1 declares `ResourceType = 'Policy'`, but MT.1041 on `main` still says `Tenant`. Jeremy's follow-up issue (`maester365/maester#2482`) was closed as completed with MT.1041 ticked, but the change never reached `main`. ORCA.118.1 on `main` is also still High, though that now matches 2.1.14.
3. **A call on LongRunning.** Jeremy removed `LongRunning` from 6.1.3 (the mailbox audit-bypass query), so that the CIS suite runs every test by default. 6.1.3 goes through every mailbox with no limit, so on a large tenant every CIS run gets much slower. I'd put the flag back. CIS-only runs would then skip 6.1.3 unless it's selected by ID.
4. **Sam's "changes requested" review is still on the PR.** Everything Sam raised is either fixed or in this list, but the review keeps the PR blocked. Sam has to re-review, or you can dismiss it.
5. **Minor, non-blocking:**
   - 6.2.1 matches accepted domains exactly, so a target on a subdomain counts as external.
   - CodeRabbit says the DMARC `rua` check misreads valid whitespace and that 2.1.8 doesn't follow chained SPF redirects.
   - The PSScriptAnalyzer warnings are about unused parameters in a test mock, which is harmless.

result.output: coderabbitai: ** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Let request exceptions reach the engine instead of reporting NotAuthorized.** `Get-MtAzureSubscriptionPolicy` catches every exception from `Invoke-MtAzureRequest` and returns `$null`. The test treats any `$null` as missing authorization and skips with `NotAuthorized`. A non-authorization exception, such as a transport failure, is therefore reported as an authorization skip. `Invoke-MtAzureRequest` returns `$null` for HTTP 401 and 403 itself, so the helper's catch is not needed for authorization handling. Removing it lets the engine record the failure as an `Error` result. ```diff - try - { - $policy = Invoke-MtAzureRequest ` - -RelativeUri '/providers/Microsoft.Subscription/policies/default' ` - -ApiVersion '2021-10-01' - } - catch { - Write-Verbose "Error retrieving subscription policy: $_" - return $null - } - - return $policy + Invoke-MtAzureRequest ` + -RelativeUri '/providers/Microsoft.Subscription/policies/default' ` + -ApiVersion '2021-10-01' ```

All CodeRabbit threads on [#2472](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2472) are resolved. Eight of the nine were already resolved before I started; they were the earlier findings that Oppedijk's commits and mine had fixed.

The ninth was a new finding on my push, and it was right. `Get-MtAzureSubscriptionPolicy` caught every exception and returned `$null`, so a network error would have been reported as "not authorized". I removed the catch block: `Invoke-MtAzureRequest` already returns `$null` on 401/403, and any other error now reaches the engine as an Error result.

- **Commit:** `d851183d1`, pushed to Oppedijk's branch.
- **Thread:** I [replied](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2472#discussion_r4400425978) with what changed and marked it resolved.

﻿No account is configured to bypass mailbox audit logging.

Audit bypass is meant for service accounts that generate a lot of noise, such as a monitoring or journaling account. Anything such an account does in any mailbox is not logged. An attacker or a malicious administrator with an account on the bypass list can read and change mail with no record in the audit log.

Remove the bypass from every account and reduce the noise in another way, for example by filtering the audit log when you search it.

#### Remediation action

1. Connect to Exchange Online with `Connect-ExchangeOnline`.
2. List the accounts with `Get-MailboxAuditBypassAssociation -ResultSize Unlimited | Where-Object { $_.AuditBypassEnabled }`.
3. For each account run `Set-MailboxAuditBypassAssociation -Identity <account> -AuditBypassEnabled $false`.

content.text:
I posted the retest request on [#2410](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2410#issuecomment-6469962842).

**[#2483](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2483)** (soulemike, AD permission model) adds a `Permission` attribute to all 270 AD tests, plus a validation test and a docs page (`website/docs/advanced/active-directory.md`). Nobody has commented on it yet.

**It fits what's already on `main`.** The format the values use (`ActiveDirectory:Ldap:user:ReadProperty`, the `Cim`, `File` and `Remoting` kinds) comes from #2500. It's in `MaesterServiceRegistry.psd1` and `writing-tests/index.mdx`. So this PR fills in values for a feature we already shipped. I think that answers the "needs decision" question, and I'd accept the approach.

**CI failures:** AD-DACL-08 to -12 return `$null` on ubuntu and macOS, and I reproduced all 5 locally. `main` already fixed this in `7bf9b9e67`, and the branch doesn't have that commit, so merging `main` should clear them.

**Problems:**
1. **Wrong CIM permissions on 22 tests.** Each part of the "Cim" row below is wrong:

   | Tests | Declared | What the collector does (`Invoke-MtADManagementCommand.ps1:188-202`) |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | 19 DNS tests | `Cim:root\DNS:MicrosoftDNS_Zone:Read` | Reads `root\MicrosoftDNS`, the namespace in the registry's own example, from three classes: `MicrosoftDNS_Zone`, `MicrosoftDNS_ResourceRecord` and `MicrosoftDNS_RootHints` |
   | 3 SMB tests (AD-DC-02 to -04) | `Cim:root\SmbConfigurations:...` | Calls `Get-SmbServerConfiguration`, which uses `root\Microsoft\Windows\SMB` |

   A user who grants exactly what these tests declare will still fail those checks.
2. **The description promises more than the PR does.** It says the permissions are "dynamically derived from collector source code" and validated against "its data collection". The values are hand-written, and `ADPermissionValidation.Tests.ps1` only checks that each test has a `Permission`, that it parses, and that it starts with `ActiveDirectory:`. It never compares the values with what the collector reads, which is how the namespace errors got through.
3. **Every file loses its BOM.** All 270 test files lose their UTF-8 BOM on line 1, which accounts for the 270 deleted lines. 53 of them contain non-ASCII characters. It works on PowerShell 7, but it touches every file in the diff for no reason, and the rest of the repo keeps BOMs.

I spot-checked the LDAP values on a few tests (DOM-01, CFG-01, the DACL tests) and they look right. The shared `ReadProperty` rights are the right ones, and they fit what Authenticated Users can read by default.
Fix it ourselves
